reason: H0 parses archive entries and consumes their data but never exercises the tar verbose-listing path in list_item_verbose. The changed production logic operates on archive_entry_mtime(entry), computes age with difftime(tim, now), selects a date format using HALF_YEAR and bsdtar->day_first, and passes tim to localtime/localtime_r/localtime_s. Thus attacker-controlled archive timestamp values, including extreme or boundary mtimes, and the associated listing configuration are not covered by H0.
evidence: H0 calls archive_read_next_header and archive_read_data, then frees the archive; it never calls list_item_verbose or another visible listing/output function.
list_item_verbose obtains tim from archive_entry_mtime(entry), so archive input semantics directly influence the changed code.
The changed lines replace time_t arithmetic with age = difftime(tim, now) and compare age against HALF_YEAR, exposing boundary and extreme-time behavior worth fuzzing.
The affected path also branches on bsdtar->day_first and invokes localtime/localtime_r/localtime_s plus strftime, none of which are exercised by H0.
recommended_action: Add a tar verbose-listing harness that constructs or parses entries with fuzz-controlled mtime values and invokes list_item_verbose using initialized bsdtar state and a bounded output stream; cover extreme time_t values, values around now ± HALF_YEAR, both day_first settings, and pathname/link metadata.
